source.check: unopposed members and full names from the News-Letter's list of nominations (6 May; * = retiring member as printed there) and its list of the remaining contests after withdrawals (7 May); votes, majorities, spoiled papers and electorates read on the page image of the News-Letter's results

note: First May round under the Local Government Act (Northern Ireland) 1934 (no election in January 1935): one councillor in each of the 15 wards of Belfast Corporation (the 1932 cohort) and the eight aldermen elected in 1929 (Clifton, Court, Cromac, Dock, Falls, Shankill, Victoria, Windsor); nominations Tuesday 5 May, poll Friday 15 May 1936. After the withdrawal in Dock, 17 of the 23 seats were filled unopposed; Clifton, Court (both seats), Duncairn, Falls and Smithfield were contested (Belfast News-Letter, 6, 7 and 16 May 1936). The retiring councillor, Dr Lowe, stood against the official Unionist nominee. Brown's 3,288 is the figure both newspapers print (Belfast News-Letter, 16 May 1936, pp. 6 and 7; Irish News, 16 May 1936, p. 7) and the one the printed majority of 642 needs; the Irish News adds a total poll of 8,116 with 57 spoiled papers, which 3,288 + 2,646 + 2,125 + 57 makes exactly. The Belfast Corporation register of members (PRONI LA/7/1/CA/1/3) records 3,228, which fits neither. The News-Letter prints 51 spoiled papers, kept here.
